clue.text: Toffee say? Suck oddly covered in fluff

indicators.note: being covered in something means it wraps around the other letters, so the fluff word goes outside

parts.note: to fluff a task is to botch it
to say is to utter

indicators.note: oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word Suck

explanation.surface: A sweet suggestion: suck a toffee and you end up with fluff stuck all over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' wraps the fluff word around the rest, and 'oddly' picks letters one and three of Suck. 'say?' seems to mark Toffee as an example, but say is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle confection made from butter and brown sugar, a kind of toffee.

clue.text: Censored strip rising in sack

indicators.note: in places the reversed strip word inside the sack word

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for strip is read upwards, that is reversed

parts.note: to strip something is to peel it

explanation.surface: Someone stripping is cut from the broadcast after getting up out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the strip word upwards in this down clue, and 'in' sets it within the sack; sack is slang for bed, not a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters bleep out swear words with a tone, so a bleeped word has been censored.

clue.text: Elevated top held by dexterity?

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the built word is read from bottom to top
held by means the top word goes inside the word for dexterity

parts.note: art is skill or dexterity
A1 means top, first-class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A crown placed high on the head is kept there by skilful handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts top inside dexterity and 'Elevated' turns the result upward. A1 meaning first-class is written with an I. As a whole the clue pictures the answer: a top piece worn high and balanced with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornament worn high on top of the head, kept in place with some poise.

clue.text: He likes endless nosh in huge container

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a person: he who likes good food and pleasure

parts.note: epic means huge, on a grand scale

indicators.note: in places the shortened nosh word inside the container

parts.note: an urn is a container

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for nosh is cut off

parts.note: to nosh is to eat

explanation.surface: A man who loves eating is happy with endless food served in an enormous pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the nosh word and 'in' sets it within the container. The definition leans on nosh too: the answer is one who likes fine food.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to sensual pleasure, especially good food and drink.

clue.text: Driver's position in foreign car

definitions.meaning: A Spanish car maker, a foreign car to the British setter

explanation.definitionFit: The driver sits in a seat, and SEAT is also a Spanish make of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Miss sweetheart, left to end love, right?

indicators.note: to end says the letter for left is moved from the front to the back of the sweetheart word

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is right to give up love and part from a sweetheart they miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left to end' moves L in LOVER to the back, making OVERL.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to fail to notice it, to miss it.

clue.text: Collection of stones roughly in rink occasionally

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning roughly or about

indicators.note: occasionally asks for every other letter of the words in rink, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Curling stones are piled up rather messily on the ice rink now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to curling, but stones here are a hill marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones built up as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: Corona perhaps involving public uprising for good

indicators.note: involving means the virus word takes in the other letters

parts.note: the coronavirus is an example of a virus, marked by perhaps

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word for public is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: when news is out it is public

explanation.surface: A virus provokes a popular revolt, for the general good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reads the public word upwards and 'involving' sets it inside the virus. Corona suggests a beer or a cigar, and uprising a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuous means morally good, having high principles.

clue.text: French anger is about trade

indicators.note: is about means the words before it surround the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: French fury concerns business dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is held within French anger, from the CH at the end of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To change one thing for another is to exchange or trade it.

clue.text: Kill time, say, losing heart

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the seven-letter word for say is dropped

parts.note: to dictate is to say aloud for someone to write down

explanation.surface: An instruction to kill time, or perhaps to say so, while feeling dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops the middle letter of the seven-letter word for say. 'Kill time' reads as a phrase, but Kill alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate something is to destroy it completely, to wipe it out or kill it off.

clue.text: Celtic flag initially hoisted

parts.note: the flag, or yellow flag, is a wild iris

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word hoisted

explanation.surface: A Celtic banner is run up the flagpole.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag reads as a banner, but it is the plant: the yellow flag is a type of iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is one of the Celtic languages and peoples, so the adjective Celtic can stand for it.

clue.text: Pandemic starts to provoke lethargy with fever

indicators.note: starts to asks for the first letter of each of the next two words, provoke and lethargy

parts.note: ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: A disease outbreak begins by causing tiredness and a high temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a widespread deadly epidemic, which is what a pandemic is.

clue.text: Seafood? Bucketload put on board

indicators.note: put on means one piece is placed after the other here, the load following the board

parts.note: a plank is a long board of wood
a ton is a large amount, a bucketload

explanation.surface: A huge haul of seafood is loaded onto a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this is food for the sea's creatures, such as whales, rather than food from the sea for us.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton is the drifting mass of tiny organisms that whales and fish feed on, so it is literally food in the sea.

clue.text: Made slightly wet politician's inside backing obsolete

indicators.note: the politician is said to be inside, so those letters go within the other word
backing means the word for obsolete is read from right to left

parts.note: something obsolete is dead, no longer in use
an MP is a Member of Parliament; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone was dampened by an outdated idea held inside a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads the obsolete word backwards, and 'inside' sets the politician within it; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To damp something is to moisten it, so damped is the past tense meaning made a little wet.

clue.text: Drug practically changing Ecstasy

indicators.note: practically means almost all of it, so the last letter of the word for changing is dropped

parts.note: morphing means changing form
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug is said to be almost turning into ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' drops the final G from MORPHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is a powerful painkilling narcotic made from opium.

clue.text: Delay work, retiring, asleep finally in pit

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the short word for work is read reversed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: in places that final letter inside the word for pit

parts.note: the stone of a fruit is also called its pit

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word asleep

explanation.surface: A miner holds up work by dozing off down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the work word round, 'finally' takes the last letter of asleep and 'in' puts it within the pit word. Pit suggests a mine, but here it is a fruit's hard centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone something is to put it off until later, which is to delay it.

clue.text: Common European standard

parts.note: standard here is a flag; a three-banded national flag is common across Europe, as in France, Italy and Ireland

explanation.walkthrough: Standard looks like a norm or regulation, as in an EU rule, but it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a flag of three colours in bands, the design of many European national flags.

clue.text: Long to comprehend setter's restraint, almost amusing

indicators.note: to comprehend means to take in, so the long word holds the other letters

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the restraint word is dropped

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, restrained on a leash

explanation.surface: A setter longs to understand why the crossword's compiler is so restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from the restraint and 'to comprehend' has the long word take it in. Setter looks like the puzzle's compiler but is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasant is agreeable and enjoyable, close to amusing or entertaining.

clue.text: Intensely good man mistakenly mislaying wife …

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: mislaying means the letter for wife is lost from the word for mistakenly

parts.note: to do something mistakenly is to do it wrongly

explanation.surface: A good man feels strongly that he has wrongly lost his wife, a story continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaying' takes W from WRONGLY to leave RONGLY. The ellipsis just links the surface to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel something strongly is to feel it with great force, that is intensely.

clue.text: It's plain sweetheart's rejected exercise

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the sweetheart word is read reversed

parts.note: a pet is a sweetheart, and sweetheart's is read as the plural pets
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: It is clear that someone's darling has turned down a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' sends the sweetheart word back. It's plain reads as it's obvious, but plain is a noun: an expanse of flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland, as in Siberia, which is a plain.

clue.text: … wife commonly lets go, we hear

definitions.note: commonly marks a colloquial word, the informal name for one's wife

indicators.note: we hear says the word for lets go is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to miss an opportunity is to let it go, so lets go is misses

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the wife walks out on us.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is the informal, working-class term a man uses for his spouse.

clue.text: Reportedly East Ender's seeing that present open

indicators.note: Reportedly East Ender's says the phrase is spoken as a Cockney would say it, dropping the H and running the words together

parts.note: seeing that is since and present is here, giving since here

explanation.surface: It is said that a Londoner, since being here, is open and honest about the gift.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders are Cockneys from east London, who famously drop the letter H, so here comes out as 'ere.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person is open and genuine, free from pretence.

clue.text: Part of atmosphere there, almost rarefied

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the atmosphere up there is thin, nearly airless.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the final E of atmosphere through there into the start of almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means light, delicate and airy, as is anything rarefied or refined beyond the earthly.

clue.text: One reigns, usually leading extensive region, principally

definitions.text: One reigns, usually leading extensive region, principally

indicators.note: principally asks for the principal, that is first, letter of each of the five words reigns to region

explanation.surface: A monarch typically governs a wide territory as its head.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a monarch, and the first letters of reigns, usually, leading, extensive and region spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a sovereign, someone who reigns over and leads a realm.

clue.text: Contagion spot with risk gone discovered

indicators.note: discovered is read as dis-covered, with the covers or outer letters removed from spot, risk and gone

explanation.surface: An infection is detected once the danger has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' means stripped of its covering: take the first and last letters off spot, risk and gone to leave PO, IS and ON. 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Contagion in its older sense means a corrupting or poisonous influence, so poison fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Offspring fostering hundred and one offspring

indicators.note: fostering means taking in and caring for, so the son word holds the other letters

parts.note: a son is an offspring
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child fosters a hundred and one other children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fostering' puts C plus I inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a descendant or heir, a child of a family.

clue.text: Flipping bonkers essay!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word for bonkers is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, bonkers

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a crazy piece of homework.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping looks like a mild expletive, but it signals the turnaround. Essay is not a composition but a try.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to attempt it, and an essay is an old word for an attempt.

clue.text: Disciplinary board centre in recess

indicators.note: recess means going back, so only the central three letters of the board word are turned round

parts.note: a board of people, such as interviewers, is a panel

explanation.surface: A disciplinary committee sits in the middle of the holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre in recess' reverses only the middle ANE of PANEL, giving ENA between P and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal relates to punishment, so a penal measure is a disciplinary one.

clue.text: Empower American God, one constrained by good

indicators.note: constrained by means the god and the one are held inside the word for good

parts.note: use means good or benefit, as in no use for no good
Thor is the Norse god of thunder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An American is given power by a god, though held back by goodness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constrained by' sets the god and the one inside the word for good; use means good as in it's no use.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise someone is to give them official permission or power to act.

clue.text: Lump of old potato with caper dressing

indicators.note: dressing means the caper word is wrapped around the old and potato pieces like clothing

parts.note: to caper is to prance about
a potato is a tuber

explanation.surface: A lumpy old potato is served with a caper sauce on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' wraps the caper word around old plus potato. Caper and dressing suggest a sauce, but caper is a frisky leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A protuberance is something that sticks out, a swelling, bulge or lump.
